orders.text:
Time Extension Application (CLMA No. 1545 of 2020)
In
CLR No. 109 of 2018
Hon’ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Ankit Shah, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Deepak Bisht, Advocate, holding brief of 
Mr. K.K. Harbola, Advocate for respondent.

accordingly.

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS 
10.03.2021 CLR No.109 of 2018 
Hon’ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Ankit Shah, Advocate, for the 
revisionist. 
 Mr. K.K. Harbola, Advocate, for the 
respondent. 
 
 This is a tenant’s revision, which has been 
preferred under Section 25 of the Provincial 
Small Causes Court Act, as well as against the 
decree, which was rendered on 13.09.2018 in 
SCC No.23 of 2011 “MDDA Remki Vs. Shri 
M.L. Chamoli”. 
 The revision has been admitted. 
 A statement has been made by the learned 
counsel for the revisionist at the bar that the 
execution proceedings preferred by the 
respondent has already been rejected, for which 
the learned counsel for the respondent prays that 
the matter may be adjourned in order to file an 
appropriate revision, as against the rejection of 
his execution proceedings. 
 The matter is adjourned. 
 List this matter after two weeks. 
 
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 
 10.03.2021 
NR/

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CLR No. 109 of 2018
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. None for the revisionist.
2. Mr. K.K. Harbola, learned counsel for the 
respondent.
3. The judgment and order passed by the Trial 
Court was stayed subject to the condition that the 
revisionist shall deposit the entire decretal amount 
before the court below on or before 28.03.2019 and 
continues to pay of sum of Rs. 20,000/- per month to 
the respondent for use and occupation of the shop in 
question w.e.f. February, 2019.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent submits that 
the condition as stipulated in order dated 07.03.2019 
was never been complied with by the revisionist and 
thereafter the time extension application was moved by 
the revisionist and six weeks further time was granted 
by the Coordinate Bench, despite this, the order has not 
been complied with.
5. Since the order has not been complied with, Mr. 
K.K. Harbola, who appears for the respondent, on 
instructions, apprise to this court that the condition as 
stipulated by the Coordinate Bench has not been 
complied with and the revisionist is enjoying the 
interim order passed in the year 2019.
6. Since, the learned counsel for the revisionist is 
not present today.
7. Put up this matter on 17.12.2025 on top of Board.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 15.12.2025
PR

Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. B.S. Adhikari, Advocate for the 
revisionist.
2. Mr. K.K. Harbola, Advocate for the 
respondent.
3. Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate for the 
MDDA.
4. It has been informed that the possession 
of the shop in question was already handed 
over to the respondent. The respondent was 
the contractor of the MDDA. The dispute as on 
date is only with regard to the arrears of the 
rent which according to the respondent is 
about Rs.70 lakhs. Since the respondent was 
the contractor of the MDDA and on the 
previous date, both the parties were asked to 
appear before this Court for resolving the 
dispute amicably, but due to some problem, 
they could not appear. Therefore, this Court is 
of the view that both the parties may appear 
before the Vice Chairman of the MDDA within 
10 days apprise all facts to the Vice Chairman 
and Vice Chairman may make efforts in 
between both the parties. 
5. Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate shall inform 
about this order to Vice Chairman.
6. Put up on 09.01.2026.
 (Rakesh Thaplial, J.) 
 23.12.2025
